info.title: Andaru local engine API
info.description: Experimental engine API over separate kernel-peer-gated Unix sockets. UID 0 retains the root-local API; the dedicated web UID receives only authenticated browser/token routes plus login and setup-required status. Network status is observed; configuration and restore writes create durable saved versions and never activate networking. Contracts remain provisional until Andaru 1.0.

x-andaru-web-peer-uid: Exact non-root UID configured at engine startup; accepted only on the separate web socket before HTTP parsing.

get.summary: Follow the events that change what the web UI shows, as Server-Sent Events
get.description: Each event is one data line holding the event bus's JSON payload (id, type, time, source, data): config.head.changed when a new head is saved and apply.changed when an apply changes state, for callers with configuration.read; notifications.changed when the active notifications change, for callers with notifications.read. Events are not kept: a client reads the state when the stream opens and again at every event. A comment line arrives every 25 seconds; the stream ends within that time of its session ending or of a change in the capabilities it was opened with, and a stream that falls behind is closed. Opening or keeping the stream does not count as activity for the session's idle timeout.

400.description: A query string, a request body, or a session cookie together with an Authorization header

403.description: The account has neither configuration.read nor notifications.read

get.summary: Read the last hour of every network interface's counters
get.description: The engine reads every interface but the loopback every intervalSeconds, 5 today, and keeps the last hour in memory. The history starts again when the engine does. Counters are cumulative: a client works out a rate from neighbouring samples and treats a counter that went down as a gap. An interface that has gone keeps its samples until they are an hour old. A client reads the hour once, then asks with since for what it lacks.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: The at of the newest sample the client holds, as served. Only samples after it are sent; every interface is still named, with an empty list when it has nothing newer. A since later than every sample held is answered with the whole history and complete true

400.description: since is not one time in the form the samples carry, or the query holds anything else

get.description: A raise dated later than when the engine recorded it is dated then. A notification that requires another capability is listed only for callers that have it as well. The list changes as sources raise and clear notifications and as they are dismissed; the event stream carries notifications.changed after each change.

password.description: Required at this exact request for a non-root human session exporting secrets or credentials

RestoreMultipart.description: Exactly these two parts. Total HTTP body limit is 18956288 bytes; parts are held only in bounded memory.

time.description: The box's clock at the reading

cpu.description: Tick counters summed over all processors since boot. Busy over a period is one minus the growth of idle over the growth of total

load.description: The load averages over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, all three; null when the kernel does not give them

availableBytes.description: What programs can still get without swapping, by the kernel's estimate

fileSystems.description: File systems on a device or a ZFS pool, each device and each pool once: as / or /var when it is mounted there, else at its shortest mount point. FUSE mounts are left out

availableBytes.description: What an unprivileged writer can still use

connections.description: The connection-tracking table; null while the kernel tracks no connections

sensor.description: The chip's name and, where it names its inputs, the input's label

intervalSeconds.description: How often the engine reads the counters

complete.description: True when the answer is the whole history, which replaces what the client holds; false when it is samples to add

samples.description: Oldest first, at most an hour, or what came after since

version.description: The Andaru version that serves this

architecture.description: As the kernel names it, such as x86_64 or aarch64

time.description: The box's clock at the request

bootedAt.description: When the kernel started, the kernel's own whole second; null when it does not say

memoryBytes.description: The memory the kernel has to use, a little less than what is installed

guest.description: The hypervisor when the box is a virtual machine; empty on hardware

iommu.description: Whether the kernel has devices behind an active IOMMU

model.description: Empty where the kernel names none, as on most arm64 machines

cores.description: Online cores; equal to threads where the kernel names no cores

microcode.description: The revision the kernel loaded, not the one on disk

level.description: The x86-64 microarchitecture level; empty on other architectures

features.description: The CPU features a firewall gains from, each by its usual name and only when every online processor has it

vulnerabilities.description: The kernel's own report, one entry per known CPU vulnerability

state.description: A reading of the status: vulnerable when the kernel says so anywhere in the line, unknown for anything it words otherwise

hardware.description: From the firmware's DMI table. The serial is the product's, or the board's when the product has none. A field the vendor left as a placeholder is empty

requested.description: The requested prefix length; 0 when none is requested.

ifIndex.description: Observed kernel index; not persistent identity

operState.description: Observed tool state, including UNKNOWN where reported

linkAddress.description: Current link-layer address if supplied, not a permanent MAC promise

kind.description: Kernel link kind (vlan, bridge, bond, veth, ...); omitted for a physical device

permanentAddress.description: Hardware address the device cannot change, which saved Ethernet links name; a virtual link reports the one it inherits or its current address

address.description: Host IP address, not a network-masked prefix

WebPreferences.description: Any one JSON object of at most 16 KiB as sent, with unique member names and valid UTF-8, kept per account. Its content is the client's; the engine acts on nothing in it. It is in no backup.

details.description: Safe field errors with request-relative JSON Pointers; empty for non-field failures.

findings.description: Why an apply was refused (APPLY_REFUSED only).

version.description: The list's version after this save; the next If-Match is "order.<version>".

order.description: The rule IDs in the order this request saved.

writtenBy.description: The Andaru version that saved this version; absent when the Andaru that saved it did not record it.

questions.description: The decisions this version needs to read in the current schema. It reads with the provisional choices until they are answered.

choices.description: A choice ID for each question ID answered so far.

expectedSavedVersion.description: The head the questions were worked out from; required to save.

provisional.description: The choice the settings read with while nobody has answered.

objects.description: The IDs of the objects the decision is about.

choice.description: The choice this reading used: the answer given, or the provisional one.

interface.description: Kernel interface currently carrying that permanent MAC

path.description: Destination a later apply would write

secret.description: True when the real file holds a secret; content then shows <redacted> in its place

sources.description: JSON Pointers into the saved snapshot value

path.description: JSON Pointer into the saved snapshot value; empty for host-wide findings

state.description: Never saved, applied or live state

realizable.description: True when no finding is an error

savedVersion.description: Must be the saved head: the version the operator previewed.

confirmTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds until the change is rolled back unless confirmed.

state.description: awaiting_confirmation is live but will be rolled back at the deadline; only confirmed survives a reboot.

previous.description: What was live before this apply; null is no generation.

reason.description: Why the apply failed or was rolled back, or what remains to finish at the next boot; empty otherwise.

files.description: Files of this generation; their content is shown by the preview.

lastKnownGood.description: The generation confirmed before it; boot falls back to it.

pending.description: The apply awaiting confirmation, if any.

live.description: What runs now; null is no generation (the bare filter, and the catch-all once set up). Differs from confirmed after a boot fallback.

path.description: What the finding is about: a JSON Pointer into the saved snapshot value, an interface name, a systemd unit name or a host file path; empty for host-wide findings.

id.description: Names this notification until it ends, for dismissing it

source.description: What raised it: applies, upgrade, disk, notifications, an add-on

key.description: What it is about, unique within its source, such as apply/12

detail.description: A few lines of plain text

link.description: A path in the web UI where it can be acted on, such as /changes

requires.description: The capability, besides notifications.read, needed to see it

updated.description: When it was raised or last changed

Forbidden.description: Missing, unverified or non-root Unix peer; JSON error for GET, no body for HEAD

InventoryUnavailable.description: Command, parsing, size or deadline failure; never a partial success
